title: Quincy Holdings — Partnership diligence & outbound drafts
content:
Top-level notes (quick mental model):
- Quincy Holdings = mid-size alternative asset manager (hedge + credit funds). HQ NYC, ~220 employees (est). Heavy use of proprietary research + compliance controls.
- Likely priorities: data residency, auditability, model quality for research assistants, cost predictability for batch/overnight workloads, integrations with Snowflake + internal data stores.
- Competitive signals: job postings for "ML infra" and "data platform" (passed), they run AWS primarily (S3, EMR mention in job reqs).

Key contacts (scraped + inferred):
- Eva Morales — Head of Platform Engineering (VP) — LinkedIn: eva-morales-qh. PRIMARY.
- Samir Patel — Director, Quant Research — potential champion for model-driven research assistants.
- Daniel Reed — Legal/Compliance counsel (GDPR/SEC filings).
- SDR/BD touch: Marcus Li (intro via mutual HashiCorp connection).

Account risks / red flags:
- Strong compliance posture — likely resist hosted multi-tenant unless we can get SOC2 + contract-level data residency + audit logs.
- Existing tooling: in-house search portal and internal notebook infra. May perceive replacing infra as high-friction.
- Budget cycle: looks like Q3 procurement window — timeline may stretch.

Primary use cases to pitch (ordered by acceptance risk / impact):
1) Research assistant for analysts (summaries, literature retrieval, citation generation). Low-latency not critical; quality & audit trails important. Good fit for Redwood Private or Dedicated.
2) KYC / client onboarding triage (sensitive PII) — requires private deployment + strict KMS.
3) Automated meeting notes + CRM sync (Salesforce) — mid acceptance, need connector proof-of-concept.
4) Embeddings for internal knowledge graph (Snowflake -> vector DB) — standard ask; highlight cost savings via batching/caching.

Tech notes (things to confirm in discovery):
- Data gravity: where are their corp data stores? Snowflake? S3 buckets? Internal PG clusters?
- Current model usage: Are they running any LLMs in prod? If yes, which families (LLAMA, Mistral, Anthropic)?
- Latency SLO expectations: for research assistant likely <1s token latency not required, but interactive chat should stay under 200-400ms for good UX.
- Security gateways: inbound/outbound firewall policies, IP whitelisting, private peering.

Outbound messaging (email variant A - concise):
Subject: Proof-of-concept for private LLM inference at Quincy Holdings
Hi Eva —
I’m Asha on the partnerships team at Redwood Inference. We help infra teams run LLM inference with predictable latency, strong audit logs, and private deployment options that preserve residency/KMS controls.
We’ve helped other asset managers run research assistants and KYC triage in a VPC/on-prem setup — typically pilot in 4–6 weeks.
Are you open to a 20-minute intro next week to see if a pilot might fit Quincy’s procurement/timeline?
Best,
Asha

Email variant B — technical-first (for Samir):
Subject: Reduce inference cost for research workflows (batch + cache)
Samir —
Quick note: Redwood’s serving runtime supports automatic prefix caching and workload-aware batching that reduced tokens/cost ~3x for a quant research workflow we benchmarked. If you have overnight batch jobs or notebook-backed inference, a short pilot shows measurable unit-cost wins. Any chance for a 30-min walkthrough?

LinkedIn DM (short):
Hi Eva — noticed Quincy recently posted for "platform engineering" roles. I lead partnerships at Redwood Inference — we help infra teams run private LLM inference with audit logs + KMS integration. Can I send a 1-pager?

Cold call script (30s):
Hi Eva — this is Asha from Redwood Inference. We help companies like Quincy run private, auditable LLM inference with predictable performance. I realize you likely get a lot of outreach — are you the right person for a quick chat on private LLM pilots, or should I connect with someone on your platform team?

Objection handling (cheat sheet):
- "We can just host open models ourselves" -> empathize: "Totally — many teams start with self-hosting. Typical blockers are ops maintenance, kernel/quantization tuning, and cost unpredictability. Redwood provides the runtime + ops patterns so your platform team can avoid the repeated tuning and unlock predictable unit economics."
- "Data residency/PII concerns" -> response: "We offer private deployment (VPC or on-prem) with KMS/HSM integration and per-request audit logs. We can also run an air-gapped proof-of-concept if needed for legal review."
- "We care about model fidelity / hallucinations" -> response: "We surface prompt/eval tooling and continuous regression alerts tied to your eval sets; we also support model pinning and staged rollouts so you can rollback if quality regresses."
- "Cost is too high" -> response: "Start with a narrow pilot: research assistant for a single desk or embeddings for a single dataset. Our Optimize toolkit identifies batching/quantization profiles that often reduce per-token cost by 2–4x without measurable quality loss."

Suggested pilot structure (45–60 days):
- Week 0–1: Kickoff + access & compliance checklist (legal, network).
- Week 1–2: Private deployment (staging VPC) + connect to sample data (Snowflake/S3).
- Week 3–4: Integrate into one team workflow (research or KYC) + basic dashboards (latency, token cost).
- Week 5–6: QA + business review + success metrics (reduction in analyst time or cost per query).

Metrics to lock early (examples to request from Quincy):
- Current avg tokens per research query and queries/day by desk
- Baseline cost (cloud GPU or third-party API) per 1000 queries
- SLA expectations (uptime, p95 latency)
- Compliance checklist items (SOC2? ISO? data residency requirements)

Open questions to answer in discovery (internal):
- Who in procurement signs off on pilots < $50k? (Get name + procurement cycle)
- Will they accept contractor NDA vs. full SOW?
- Any policy on model weights licensing (open weights OK?)

Admin TODOs (my next steps):
- [ ] Draft 1-pager tailored to Quincy (focus on private deployment + research assistant case study) — target by 2026-02-24.
- [ ] Ask Tom to pull any previous hedge-fund / asset manager anonymized case studies for deck.
- [ ] Book intro with Eva via Marcus Li intro — tentative for week of 2026-02-27.
- [ ] Prepare privacy/compliance checklist and stub contract language for legal review.

Notes to self (loose ideas):
- Consider bringing in Solutions Eng (Priya) for early technical scoping call — focus on Snowflake->vector pipeline and KMS keyflow.
- If they push back on hosted API, emphasize Dedicated vs Private pricing comparison (predictable throughput).

Rough snippets to paste into Confluence page later:
- "Quincy pilot hypothesis: Private inference deployment for research assistant will reduce analyst query time by 15–25% and cut inference unit cost by 30% through batching and prefix caching."
- "Key departure criteria: successful audit of request logs, integration with Quincy KMS, and measurable analyst time savings in a 6-week pilot."

End of notes.
